    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — trade tensions, weak domestic demand, slipping business confidence
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural demand weakness, geopolitical risks, GDP deceleration trajectory

Synopsis:
    China's Caixin Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.5 in August (vs. 50.9 in July), beating the 51.0 consensus. Output, new orders and export orders all accelerated. However, employment stalled, output prices were cut for the first time this year amid intense competition, and business confidence softened to its weakest since January. GDP growth slowed sharply to 4.3% in Q2 from 5.0% in Q1, the weakest in over three years. Domestic demand weakness and external headwinds (trade tensions, geopolitical risk) remain material drags on the broader recovery.
